sentences.english_text: Drippy had no idea that he was about to be rescued by the cricket.
He lay on his towel in the laundry room, wondering what is going to happen next.
He did not have to wait long to find out.
A laundry truck had come to the jail to pick up all the dirty laundry.
As the cricket was moving toward Drippy's cell to save him, the laundry man was throwing the towel with Drippy on it into the back of the truck, along with sheets and towels and pillowcases.
The door of the truck closed, and the truck started off.
Well, at least I'm out of jail, Drippy thought, and Drippy was very happy.
He did not know that in another few moments he would have been saved and taken back to his mother.
Drippy had no idea where the truck was going, but he hoped it would go very far away from the police station.
If the police did not arrest him for robbing a bank, they would probably arrest him for impersonating a teardrop from the statue of the saint.
Either way, I'm in trouble, Drippy thought.
The laundry truck was traveling down a large highway, going 40 miles an hour, when the most incredible thing happened.
The truck slowly began to rise in the air.

Now, for those of you who have heard of cyclones, what happened is not really so incredible, for cyclones are very special, evil winds that twist around in a mad circle and pick up everything in its reach from the ground and toss it high in the air.
The driver frantically tried to control the truck and bring it back on the ground again, but nobody in the world can control a cyclone.
The truck was spinning around dizzily.
Poor Drippy, in the back of the truck, had no idea what was happening to him.
He climbed up to the window and looked out, and what he saw made his eyes open wide.
